extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and trademark/IP professionals who use WIPO trademark statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and using WIPO trademark statistical tables and charts (definitions, metrics, and data-quality cautions) for analysis and comparison across offices and time. Focuses on how counts, rates and categories are defined and reported in the WIPO WIPI 2020 trademark chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registrations in force (definition and interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to the number of trademark registrations in force, not the number of classes specified in those registrations. Trademark rights can be maintained indefinitely by paying renewal fees at defined intervals. Trademarks in force provide information on the volume of trademark registrations currently active, as well as the historical trademark life cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 146 IP offices. Use this metric to gauge active trademark volume rather than class-level activity. Be aware that renewals allow marks to remain indefinitely, so 'in force' reflects maintenance behavior as well as original filing activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth rate (%) (year-on-year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Growth rate shown in figures as percentage change (e.g., year-to-year growth for trademark registrations in force or Madrid applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreted as the percent change from the previous period (figure labels show 'GROWTH RATE (%)'). When comparing growth rates across offices, see caution about harmonization of procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of registrations in force by registration year (calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as follows: the number of trademark registrations issued in year t and in force in 2019 divided by the total number of trademark registrations issued in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric (used in B39) indicates survival/maintenance of registrations from a given registration year up to 2019. Based on about 15.8 million active registrations reported by 77 offices; detailed data for some large offices (e.g., China, Japan) are not available—interpret accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of trademarks in force (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average age of trademarks in force at selected offices (reported for 2014 and 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess the vintage distribution of active marks. Differences across offices can reflect renewal behaviour, national filing patterns, and data availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark examination outcomes categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of trademark examination outcomes is reported in categorical outcomes: REGISTERED, TOTAL REJECTION, WITHDRAWN/ABANDONED (as shown in B41).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcome categories allow comparing the end-results of examination processes across offices. Because application processing procedures differ across offices, use caution when comparing outcome shares between offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark examination duration (first office action and final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of trademark examination reported as average time (days) to FIRST OFFICE ACTION and to FINAL DECISION for selected offices (B44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two time-to-event metrics are shown: time to first office action and time to final decision. Differences across offices reflect procedural variations; exercise caution in cross-office benchmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark applications pending (count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of trademark applications pending for selected offices (B42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending counts give a snapshot of backlogs; compare absolute pending counts and pending per examiner or per filings to contextualize workload. Cross-office comparisons should account for procedural differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of trademark examiners (headcount)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of trademark examiners for selected offices (reported in B43).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examiner headcount to contextualize volumes, pending backlogs, or time-to-decision metrics. Note that job scope and responsibilities may vary across offices; headcount alone is not a measure of capacity or productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party oppositions (pre- and post-registration counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party oppositions reported by timing: PRE-REGISTRATION, POST-REGISTRATION, and TOTAL (B45).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts by office (and totals by country) indicate oppositions activity. Consider legal regime differences (e.g., opposition windows) when comparing across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals against decisions (counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals against decisions reported as counts for selected offices (B46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal counts reflect post‑decision dispute activity; interpretation requires understanding of an office's appeals procedures and whether appeals are counted at different levels of jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madrid System metrics: Madrid international applications (trend and origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Madrid international applications trend (annual counts and growth rates) and maps/tables of Madrid applications by origin (based on country of applicant’s address), and designation counts by Madrid member (B47–B50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts are based on the country of the applicant’s address, not the office of origin. Designation counts and origin counts are useful to analyze international filing behaviour. Note that where only Madrid designation data are available, application class counts by office/origin may be incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/Registration class counts by office and origin (Total / Resident / Non-resident)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical tables provide application class count by office and by origin broken down into Total, Resident and Non‑resident components (tables B51–B52).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resident vs non-resident breakdowns help distinguish domestic from foreign filing activity. Be aware of footnotes that alter definitions for specific offices (e.g., Benelux and EUIPO resident definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin definition for origin-based counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin is defined as the country/territory of the stated residence of the applicant in an international application. Counts are based on the country of the applicant’s address, not the office of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this origin definition when interpreting origin maps and origin tables; do not confuse applicant origin with filing office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office‑specific resident definition exceptions (Benelux, EUIPO, Netherlands territories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident applications include those filed by residents of Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands for Benelux Office; resident applications include those filed by residents of EU member states for EUIPO. The Netherlands has extended Madrid Protocol application coverage to Curacao and Sint Maarten, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing resident counts across offices, apply these office-specific notes to correctly interpret resident vs non-resident splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data harmonization caution and comparability limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from IP offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. However, due to differences in application processing procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized. Therefore caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit warning to analysts: procedural differences (e.g., examination rules, recording practices, class counting conventions, availability of detailed breakdowns) can bias direct comparisons. Adjust analyses or apply harmonization methods where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing / not applicable codes (.. and n.a.)
rubrics_metrics.description: n.a. indicates not applicable. .. indicates not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect these codes when filtering or aggregating tables. '..' is a data unavailability marker distinct from 'n.a.' which denotes that a concept does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madrid designation-only data limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Madrid designation data are available therefore application class count by office and origin data may be incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For jurisdictions where only Madrid designation data are reported, full application/registration class counts may be underestimated or incomplete; exercise caution in cross‑jurisdiction totals or shares that rely on complete reporting.
